evidence.title: METHOD CARD group_softmax: same-user group softmax loss and temperature scaling (logits=[pos,neg]/temperature; loss=-log_softmax(logits)[0])

evidence.title: Same-user Group Softmax (listwise loss): logits=[pos, neg1..negK]/temperature; loss=-log_softmax(logits)[0] with gradients softmax(logits)-one_hot(pos).

evidence.title: METHOD CARD multi_task: ESMM-style auxiliary losses over shared FM embeddings; loss = ranking_loss + aux_weight * BCE(play_time/is_click/etc.); safe fixed aux_weight grid and cautions about auxiliary-gradient swamping (start 0.05–0.3; disable play_time first if needed).

discoveries.hypothesis: Adding a very low-weight play_time auxiliary head alongside click-only supervision (fixed aux_weight, no ramp) will improve long_view representation quality and top-5 ordering by transferring shared embedding signal from higher-frequency engagement events without swamping the ranking gradients.
discoveries.rationale: ESMM-style multi-task sharing is expected to regularize embeddings, and the method card flags auxiliary swamping as the key failure mode—so we keep aux_weight minimal and avoid any unverified training schedules while changing only the set of auxiliary heads.

evidence.title: Entire Space Multi-Task Model (ESMM) / multi-task shared-supervision argument (auxiliary signals improve representation under related behaviours)
Kit guidance: multi-task is the highest-priority untested direction after ranking-loss families

discoveries.hypothesis: Jointly training the long_view ranking backbone with a shared auxiliary click head and a low-weight play_time head using a linear aux_weight ramp will improve within-user top-5 ordering (nDCG@5) by steering embeddings toward sustained engagement without letting auxiliary gradients dominate early.
discoveries.rationale: Compared to prior multi_task attempts, this targets the same shared-representation mechanism but replaces rare/sparse auxiliaries with a higher-frequency click signal plus a weak continuous watch-time proxy while mitigating swamping via a schedule.

evidence.title: KuaiRand METHOD CARD multi_task: weighted auxiliary BCE over same shared FM embeddings with aux targets from build_aux_labels; warns about aux_weight swamping and suggests low aux_weight starting points
Entire Space Multi-Task Model (ESMM) motivates sharing representations across correlated post-click behaviours

discoveries.hypothesis: Adding a small click+comment auxiliary BCE supervision (shared FM embeddings) with a warm-start protocol—start with click-only aux for the first few epochs, then enable the comment head for the remaining training—will improve within-user long_view top-5 ranking without swamping the ranking objective.
discoveries.rationale: It increases representation learning using related behaviours (click/comment) while controlling gradient interference via a staged auxiliary activation, which directly targets nDCG@5-sensitive ordering changes.

concerns: Warm-start / epoch-dependent enabling of the comment auxiliary head is not specified in the multi_task method card and may be infeasible or incorrectly implemented under the trusted FMRanker training abstraction.
Parameter mismatch: the proposal sets use_is_comment=false while claiming it will later enable is_comment; without explicit scheduling support, the intended head may never train.

Attribution/protocol risk: the recommended ablation sequence (click-only control first, then add comment) is merged into one experiment, making it harder to tell whether any gain/loss is due to comment supervision or general regularization/optimization effects.
rejection.next_focus: Do one bounded probe that is contract-consistent: (1) run click-only auxiliary BCE (use_is_click=true, use_is_comment=false, others false) as the control, then (2) run a separate probe enabling only is_comment (use_is_click=false or keep fixed per the method-card’s incremental ablation rule) with the same aux_weight/budget. If you want warm-start, you must explicitly define a supported mechanism in candidate.py that truly changes head activation/aux_weight over epochs within the allowed training-loop abstraction (and confirm it matches the trusted builder’s capabilities).
rejection.rationale: The proposal relies on a “warm-start then enable is_comment” schedule, but the provided multi_task method-card specifies only adding a weighted auxiliary BCE term with enabled heads; it does not define any epoch-dependent head activation/aux_weight scheduling. Given the candidate contract constraints (FMRanker training abstraction and only train-only aux labels via build_aux_labels), this warm-start protocol is not clearly executable in a contract-consistent way and may result in is_comment never actually contributing (parameters specify use_is_comment=false). Additionally, it combines the recommended stepwise search logic (click-only control, then incremental head add) into one non-attributable run, increasing the risk of misleading conclusions.

evidence.title: METHOD CARD multi_task: weighted auxiliary term over the same shared FM embeddings; safe start with aux_weight in {0.05,0.1,0.3,1.0} and begin with click-only then add one head at a time (click+comment).

discoveries.hypothesis: Adding a constant auxiliary BCE head for is_comment alongside is_click (shared FM embeddings) with a small aux_weight will provide extra supervision that improves within-user top-5 long_view ordering without swamping the ranking objective.
discoveries.rationale: Unlike sequential/history objectives, multi-task shares representation learning signals that are correlated with long_view (click strongly, comment weakly but complementary), and a small aux_weight is intended to avoid auxiliary-gradient dominance.

evidence.title: Entire Space Multi-Task Model: shared representation benefits from auxiliary related tasks (click/like/watch behaviors)
KDD 2018 multi-gate mixture-of-experts motivates controlling task influence to avoid harming the primary objective
Multi_task family description: aux loss is added to the ranking loss on train-only auxiliary heads built by build_aux_labels

discoveries.hypothesis: Adding a sparse second auxiliary head (is_comment) alongside is_click, with a linearly-ramped aux_weight schedule (0→aux_weight) over the first half of training, will better shape shared FM embeddings for long_view without early auxiliary-gradient swamping.
discoveries.rationale: Multi-task auxiliary supervision on related behaviors should improve the shared representation, while curriculum scheduling controls the risk that the auxiliary heads dominate the within-user ranking objective early.

evidence.title: METHOD CARD multi_task: aux loss = ranking_loss + aux_weight*BCE over enabled heads (including is_click and play_time) with cautions about aux_weight swamping ranking and play_time being weakest.

discoveries.hypothesis: Adding a tiny shared-playtime auxiliary BCE on top of click-only supervision (long_view ranking as primary) will improve within-user top-5 ordering by sharpening shared FM embeddings toward sustained-engagement signals without swamping the ranking head.
discoveries.rationale: Compared to click-only, the additional play_time supervision is correlated with long_view (but weaker than click) and should provide extra representation pressure specifically helpful for nDCG@5 when weighted conservatively.

concerns: Intent/config mismatch: hypothesis claims play_time auxiliary is enabled, but `use_play_time` is false so the play_time head cannot contribute aux loss.
Because the run will not match the described contrast, it’s unclear how the iteration informs the decision relative to the click-only control.
Epoch/early-stopping settings are not necessarily wrong, but given the configuration mismatch, the risk of wasting an iteration increases.
rejection.next_focus: Approve only after correcting the probe to match the stated hypothesis—either (a) set `use_play_time=true` (and keep aux_weight small, e.g., 0.05) for a click+play_time aux run, or (b) revise the hypothesis to be explicitly “click-only multi_task” to match `use_is_click=true` and `use_play_time=false` (the method card’s recommended first step). Prefer the click-only multi_task control first if you want a clean baseline for adding play_time afterward.
rejection.rationale: This proposal is not aligned with its stated experimental intent: it claims a “click-only supervision + play_time auxiliary” probe, but the provided parameters set `use_play_time=false`, so the run cannot include the play_time auxiliary head and cannot test the hypothesized effect. While `multi_task` itself is a valid bounded direction, the current configuration would most likely execute (at most) click-only auxiliary training, making the probe unverifiable versus the intended hypothesis.

evidence.title: METHOD CARD multi_task: weighted auxiliary BCE over shared FM embeddings; start click-only; auxiliary gradients can swamp ranking at large aux_weight; auxiliary targets are train-only via build_aux_labels.

discoveries.hypothesis: Use a linear warmup curriculum for the multi-task auxiliary BCE, ramping a small (click+comment) aux_weight from 0 to 0.15 over the first half of training to shape shared FM embeddings without early auxiliary-gradient swamping of the long_view ranking head.
discoveries.rationale: A kit-supported, strictly specified aux-weight schedule should preserve the ranking head’s early optimization while still leveraging correlated auxiliary supervision (click) plus a less-sparse second signal (comment) to improve top-5 within-user ordering (nDCG@5) and maintain GAUC.

evidence.title: Entire Space Multi-Task Model (ESMM): auxiliary task losses improve shared representation learning for post-click conversion related behaviors

discoveries.hypothesis: Ramping a small click+like auxiliary loss weight only after the FM ranking head stabilizes will better shape shared embeddings for long_view, improving nDCG@5 without letting auxiliary gradients swamp the ranking objective early.
discoveries.rationale: Compared to a constant aux_weight multi_task probe, a delayed/curriculum aux schedule should preserve within-user top-5 ordering dynamics while still leveraging ESMM-style auxiliary supervision when representations are already roughly aligned to long_view.

evidence.title: METHOD CARD history_features: hypotheses and safe initial search space; prior_days preferred; smoothing m; reserved unknown/history slot; within-user invariance notes on user-only terms

discoveries.hypothesis: Isolating the event-time order-varying history mechanisms (recency + DIN-style user_author long_view affinity) with prior_days smoothing (m=20) will improve within-user top-5 long_view ranking more than broader history bundles by avoiding dilution from mostly constant-within-user signals.
discoveries.rationale: The method card and within-user-ranking invariance state that user-only/constant terms add no intra-user ordering signal, so focusing capacity on the two explicitly order-varying groups (recency and user_author) provides a cleaner, more attribution-aligned test under leakage-safe prior_days history building.

evidence.title: METHOD CARD: history_features (prior_days smoothing, reserved unknown slot, DIN-inspired user_author, recency/video_age/tab_cross grouping)

discoveries.hypothesis: Using only event-time recency (days-since-last-long_view) plus the DIN-style user_author long_view affinity, with prior_days smoothing (m=20) and the reserved unknown-history slot, will improve within-user top-5 ordering more than adding broader history groups because these two components are the most order-varying and directly tied to near-term intent.
discoveries.rationale: The starter kit evidence suggests static/user-only features and un-ablated full history bundles are hard to attribute and may include weak/near-constant parts, so isolating recency+user_author provides a leakage-safe, mechanism-focused test under the registered history_features design.

evidence.title: History_features family: long_view-only history idea, recency and smoothed rate tables, prior_days vs leave_one_out scheme, and unknown-history reserved slot.

discoveries.hypothesis: Using only event-time, long_view-only user history encoded as discretized recency bins (1/3/7/14 days) for each user-candidate pair, with prior_days smoothing (m≈20, unknown-history as reserved slot), should increase top-5 within-user separability for long_view versus the default broader history feature bundle while avoiding leave_one_out leakage risk.
discoveries.rationale: Within-user ranking needs history-conditioned, ordering-varying signals; a focused recency-weighted history ablation isolates the most likely transferable component and reduces noise from weaker history tables.

evidence.title: METHOD CARD: group_softmax (Same-user Group Softmax) — logits/softmax loss, safe search space (K in {4,8}, temperature in {0.5,1.0,2.0}, LR in {0.0003,0.0005,0.001}, embedding dim fixed at 16, batch sizes {512,1024,2048})

discoveries.hypothesis: Using group softmax over K=8 same-user candidates with a sharper temperature (0.5) will better optimize top-5 within-user ordering for long_view than the flatter temperature regimes, improving nDCG@5 without hurting GAUC.
discoveries.rationale: Listwise softmax directly matches within-user competition among a positive and multiple same-user negatives, and lowering temperature increases gradients on the hardest rank violations (top-heavy corrections).

evidence.title: BPR pairwise ordering objective and gradient w.r.t. score difference d = s_pos - s_neg

discoveries.hypothesis: Using a temperature-scaled BPR loss softplus(-alpha*(s_pos-s_neg)) will sharpen within-user relative preference for hard same-user negatives, improving top-5 nDCG while preserving GAUC.
discoveries.rationale: BPR’s pairwise ordering gradient depends directly on the score difference magnitude; scaling it (alpha>1) should increase gradient for hard violations and better align with within-user top-k ranking.
